entities.name: Ketone-to-secondary-alcohol reduction
observations: The net transformation is Ar-C(O)-CH3 to Ar-CH(OH)-CH3; ethyl ester, amide, anisole ether, aryl chlorides, and the pre-existing stereocenter are retained.
The newly formed alcohol center may generate diastereomers because the substrate already contains a stereocenter.

entities.name: Sodium borohydride
observations: Recommended first-line reagent for reducing the aryl methyl ketone while generally preserving an ethyl ester, amide, anisole ether, and aryl chlorides.
Suggested screening conditions: 0.9-1.2 equivalents in THF/ethanol or ethanol, 0-5 °C then room temperature, with prompt quench after ketone consumption.

entities.name: Luche reduction conditions
observations: NaBH4 with CeCl3·7H2O in methanol or ethanol at low temperature is a useful second-line option for a hindered or sluggish aryl ketone.
Use approximately 1.0-1.5 equivalents NaBH4 and 1-2 equivalents CeCl3·7H2O, while monitoring possible diastereoselectivity changes.

entities.name: Reagent prioritization
observations: Prioritize NaBH4, then NaBH4/CeCl3·7H2O; cautiously consider LiBH4 if necessary.
Avoid DIBAL-H because the ethyl ester may be reduced, borane because amide reduction is possible, and conventional H2/Pd because aryl chloride dehalogenation is possible.
